title: SM-1 — Studio Full-Text Search Delivery
summary: clean Studio search inputs and rank title, headings, body text, and code terms in one document-level static index
content_html:
SM-1 — Studio Full-Text Search Delivery

Status

SM-1.0 readiness is complete and parked for implementation approval. DSI-1 — Docs Viewer Search Index v2 Delivery is the accepted common metadata-only schema, tokenizer, field-policy, whole-index rebuild, and browser-query baseline. No SM-1 production or test implementation has begun.

Complete Result

Studio Docs Viewer search returns one deterministic document result for title, section-heading, body-text, and authored code queries. Ranking strongly prefers title over headings and headings over body or code matches. Parent title, document identity, and update dates remain available as structural or display metadata but are not searchable Studio terms.

Boundary

SM-1 adds Studio headings, readable body prose, inline code, and fenced code to the common v2 inverted index. It retains parent title only as non-searchable display context, rebuilds the complete Studio search index after a search-relevant document change, and keeps result presentation compact.

It does not change the v2 schema or shared browser query path established by DSI-1, enable body text for another scope, change Catalogue Search, add snippets or highlighting, create section results or deep links, add stemming/synonyms/typo correction, index link destinations or report configuration, or introduce another tokenizer or search engine.

Studio Full-Text Search Index owns the proposed data shape, extraction boundary, ranking, representative examples, and prototype payload findings. Docs Viewer Search Tokenizer owns shared term semantics.

Delivery Steps

The verification tables are initial ceilings, not quotas. Confirm or reduce the relevant table after inspecting that step's exact owners; expand it only when implementation reveals a new credible risk and the step is updated before proceeding.

SM-1.0 — Readiness And Sequence

  • [x] Confirm DSI-1 is complete and record its accepted Studio metadata-only v2 index as the implementation and payload baseline.
  • [x] Confirm Studio heading/body/code inclusion fits the shared field-policy seam without a schema, tokenizer, runtime, or scope-name branch.
  • [x] Confirm the broad shared Markdown rendering/parsing owner can expose visible headings, prose, inline code, and fenced code while excluding non-visible configuration.
  • [x] Confirm SM-1.1 owns extraction and Studio policy, SM-1.2 owns representative acceptance and payload measurement, and neither step changes another scope.
  • [x] Record genuine extraction, scope-isolation, or payload stop conditions, then stop for implementation approval.

No executable verification is budgeted for this read-only step. The production extractor, generated Studio delta, exact file set, test changes, and final payload measurement belong to SM-1.1 or SM-1.2.

Gate: Review readiness against the completed DSI-1 baseline before any SM-1 production or test implementation begins.

Record: Completed 2026-08-13. DSI-1 is complete and closed. The accepted Studio baseline is the single docs_viewer_search_index_v2 producer in build_search.py, the flat search_fields policy in docs_scopes.json and docs_scope_config.py, the sole postings query and scorer in docs-viewer-search.js, and the existing whole-index search rebuild owned by the write service and watcher. Studio currently indexes title, parent_title, exact identity, and exact last_updated; its current generated baseline is 236 documents, 630 terms, and 140,666 raw bytes. The document table already retains identity, URL, update, parent, and display metadata independently of which fields emit postings.

The existing field-policy allowlist already contains heading, body, and code, build_search_index_v2 accepts those fields generically, and the browser query owner already intersects and scores their postings. SM-1 therefore needs only a Studio policy change: enable title, heading, body, and code, while removing parent_title, identity, and last_updated from Studio postings. Parent title remains in the document table for compact result context. Other scopes retain their explicit metadata-only field lists. No schema, tokenizer, loader, query-path, scope-name branch, or full-text mode is required.

studio/shared/python/markdown_renderer.py is the broad Markdown authority. Its common Markdown-it parser exposes heading, inline, inline-code, fence, code-block, raw-HTML, script, and style boundaries, and its HTML text projection already ignores attributes and script/style contents. The exact report-source owner in docs_report_source.py can project a validated structural report declaration away before extraction. Together these existing seams can expose non-duplicate authored headings, readable prose, inline code, and fenced code without indexing front matter, link destinations, media attributes, raw markup, report configuration, or script/style contents. SM-1.1 should add one small field-aware extraction result to that shared renderer and consume it from the current search builder; it must not read generated by-ID payloads as a second source model or duplicate report parsing.

Readiness correction 2026-08-13: parent_title is not a useful Studio full-text retrieval field because it can make every child match a broad hierarchy label without matching its own authored content. It remains display metadata only. The existing scorer's relative parent_title and body/code weights are therefore inactive for Studio and need no production change. SM-1.2 remains acceptance-only: it owns generated query evidence, deterministic rank confirmation, corpus measurements, non-Studio path comparison, and the temporary manual presentation check.

The expected SM-1.1 review shape is the existing Studio scope record, shared Markdown renderer, search builder, and their current focused Python/shared-query fixtures: roughly 100–180 production/config lines and 80–140 focused test/fixture lines, plus the regenerated Studio index and delivery evidence. Stop before absorbing the change if exact visible-source extraction would require duplicating Markdown/report/media resolution, if the shared renderer cannot separate eligible text without indexing non-visible configuration, if a schema/tokenizer/reader/cache or scope-name branch becomes necessary, if another scope or Catalogue path changes, or if the production/test shape materially exceeds this estimate. Gate outcome: ready for SM-1.1 implementation review and explicit approval; no production code, tests, prototype, implementation search build, or executable verification changed or ran during readiness. The routine docs watcher regenerated only this delivery record's existing by-ID, Recent, and metadata-only search projections.

SM-1.1 — Studio Source Extraction And Field Inclusion

  • [ ] Enable heading, body, and code fields only in Studio's shared v2 search policy.
  • [ ] Extract the authored title, non-duplicate Markdown headings, readable body prose, inline code, and fenced code through the shared Markdown rendering/parsing contract.
  • [ ] Exclude front matter other than approved display/context fields, generated markup, report-block declarations, link destinations, media paths, scripts, styles, timestamps, and punctuation-only fragments.
  • [ ] Apply the shared tokenizer without adding Studio-only normalization or query behavior.
  • [ ] Retain doc_id, viewer URL, last_updated, parent_id, and parent_title only for identity, navigation, display, rebuild ownership, or deterministic tie-breaking.
  • [ ] Make an affected Studio search build recompute the complete Studio v2 index while leaving safe document-payload builds targeted.
contract or credible risk lowest adequate evidence permanent test change? why this evidence is needed
headings, prose, inline code, and fenced code are omitted or assigned the wrong rank field focused Python builder/extractor assertions over one representative Markdown document extend the current search-builder test proves the new Studio source boundary without a browser or corpus-wide fixture
front matter, URLs, report declarations, media paths, scripts, styles, dates, or document IDs leak into ordinary terms focused negative assertions in the same representative extractor fixture extend the same test rather than add a separate exclusion suite protects privacy/noise boundaries with one owned fixture
authored technical identifiers such as docs_subscope or DOCS_VIEWER_BASE_URL diverge from the shared tokenizer add only the missing Studio examples to the accepted DSI-1 tokenizer fixture extend the shared fixture only if these cases are not already covered proves technical vocabulary without duplicating tokenizer coverage
Studio policy changes another scope's generated content exact before/after comparison of non-Studio indexes during the focused build none unless an existing scope-policy contract lacks this assertion scope isolation is a generated-output property, not a new test suite

Gate: Studio extraction and field inclusion work through the shared v2 owners, focused evidence passes, and non-Studio outputs are unchanged. Stop before acceptance and payload review.

Record: Pending. Add completed checklist items, changed owners, unexpected extraction complexity, exact commands/results, generated effects, and the gate outcome.

SM-1.2 — Query Acceptance And Payload Review

  • [ ] Rebuild the complete Studio v2 search index and record document count, vocabulary/posting counts, generation time, raw bytes, and compressed bytes against the accepted DSI-1 baseline.
  • [ ] Confirm existing title queries such as studio runtime and report block tokens retain deterministic known-item behavior.
  • [ ] Confirm representative heading, prose, and code queries such as known weak spots, compatibility key, DOCS_VIEWER_BASE_URL, and docs_subscope find the intended document.
  • [ ] Confirm a full doc_id and date-derived queries such as 2026, 08, and 13 do not match solely because of structural identity or update metadata.
  • [ ] Confirm a multi-term query intersects terms, ranking remains title → heading → body/code, and one document appears at most once.
  • [ ] Inspect representative high-frequency terms and confirm the payload remains acceptable for the local Studio route without inventing a smaller-than-baseline requirement.
  • [ ] Perform one temporary manual Studio search check for compact result presentation; do not add a permanent browser test unless a browser-only contract failure is discovered and separately approved.
contract or credible risk lowest adequate evidence permanent test change? why this evidence is needed
the generated Studio postings and shared query path disagree on representative title, heading, prose, code, negative, and multi-term queries direct query assertions against the generated Studio payload through the pure shared query owner extend the smallest accepted DSI-1 query contract; no browser test proves the end-to-end data/query contract below UI choreography
duplicate field matches produce repeated rows or unstable order one focused multi-field/multi-document ranking assertion extend the same query contract protects the stated result and tie-breaking behavior without broad ranking matrices
full text causes an unexpectedly large or malformed local payload direct JSON validation plus recorded raw/compressed measurements none this is acceptance evidence for the current corpus, not a permanent size threshold
another Docs Viewer scope or Catalogue Search changes during SM-1 exact generated/path diff inspection none ownership isolation is directly observable and needs no synthetic test
the Studio route cannot load and present the accepted index one temporary manual local-route check after lower-level evidence passes none presentation is the only remaining browser concern and does not justify retained choreography coverage

Gate: Present representative query results, payload measurements, exact generated scope, named omissions, and manual presentation outcome. Stop for code review.

Record: Pending. Add completed checklist items, measurements, exact commands/results, manual outcome, unexpected complexity, and the gate outcome.

SM-1.3 — Code Review

  • [ ] Review the bounded production, policy, test, documentation, and generated diff independently after SM-1.2 evidence.
  • [ ] Check specifically for duplicated extraction/tokenizer logic, Studio-name branching outside field policy, non-visible source leakage, rank drift, stale targeted-postings behavior, another scope's output change, and Catalogue Search ownership drift.
  • [ ] Review the test diff for duplicated cases, oversized fixtures, broad query matrices, browser choreography, broad-profile expansion, and checks without a unique regression.
  • [ ] Record every finding and its resolution or explicitly accepted omission.
  • [ ] Rerun only verification-budget rows affected by review changes, then stop for review approval.

No additional evidence category is budgeted here. A review finding may require updating the affected implementation step's table before new tests or broader checks are added.

Gate: Present actual review findings, resolutions, final bounded diff, remaining risks, and affected reruns before closeout.

Record: Pending. Add findings by severity, resolutions, affected reruns, and the gate outcome.

SM-1.4 — Closeout And Durable Transfer

  • [ ] Confirm the complete result and every completion claim against the accepted implementation, acceptance, and review records.
  • [ ] Update Docs Viewer Search with the shipped Studio extraction, field-inclusion, ranking, payload, and extension contract.
  • [ ] Update Document Identity only if the distinction between structural identity and human search needs a durable clarification.
  • [ ] Mark SM-1 complete and leave Analysis full-text adoption as the separate public extension decision.
  • [ ] Present the retain-or-retire recommendation for the search feature, concepts, and deliveries without deleting them.

No implementation retest is automatic at closeout. Run only documentation projection checks made necessary by the closeout edits.

Gate: Stop for explicit closeout approval.

Record: Pending. Add durable destinations, status changes, named omissions, closeout-only evidence, and the gate outcome.
